questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: A tanker is 40 nm from land, proceeding en route, ODME operational, and discharge limits are within requirements.  Is discharge permitted?

questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: A tanker is outside a special area, more than 50 nm from land, proceeding en route, ODME operational, discharge rate within limits and total quantity within limits. Is discharge permitted?

questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: A ship discharges machinery space bilge water through an OWS. The oil content is 20 ppm. Is this permitted?

questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: A tanker is more than 50 nm from land and meets all discharge limits, but is not proceeding en route. Is discharge permitted?
options: No, vessel must be en route

questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: A tanker transfers oily mixture from cargo pump room bilges to a slop tank. The vessel is not in a special area, is more than 50 nm from land, proceeding en route, ODME operational, and discharge rate and quantity are within limits. Is discharge permitted?
options: Yes, discharge is permitted under these conditions

questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: A ship is in a Special Area, proceeding en route, and discharges machinery space bilge water through approved OWS at 15 ppm. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, if more than 50 nm from land

questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: A tanker is discharging oily water from slop tanks and the ODME fails during discharge. What is required?

questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: After completing a discharge of machinery space bilge water, the entry in the Oil Record Book is not signed by the officer in charge or the Master. Is this compliant?
options: Only Chief Engineers signature is required

questions.subject: Marine Operations
questions.question: A ship discharges oil or oily mixture in Antarctic waters. Is this permitted?
